The UK’s largest Harry Potter shop is to open in London’s Oxford Street in November, Warner Bros has announced.

The flagship store, spanning more than 21,000 square feet over two floors, will open its doors within The Ribbon development at 134-140 Oxford Street on November 4.

Inspired by the magical shopping street Diagon Alley, the new shop will become the second official Harry Potter retail destination in the UK after a site at King’s Cross Station.

Warner Bros said the destination will boast themed spaces designed to immerse fans in Harry Potter’s wizarding world, with attractions including a Ukrainian Ironbelly Dragon towering over the Gringotts area of the store, a full-sized Knight Bus, and The Leaky Cauldron wizarding pub where visitors will have the opportunity to enjoy food and Butterbeer drinks.

open image in gallery The UK’s largest Harry Potter shop, which is set to open in London’s Oxford Street in November (Mike World Wide/PA) ( PA Media )

Warner Bros has released official concept artwork for the shop, offering fans a first glimpse of the destination ahead of its opening.

Karl Durrant, Warner Bros senior vice president of worldwide retail, said: “Following the success of our Harry Potter shops around the globe, opening the Harry Potter Shop in London is a truly special milestone.

“We’re incredibly proud to bring the magic back to the city where Harry Potter’s story began.

“There’s no better place to create a destination that celebrates the magic, creativity and storytelling that has captivated generations of fans around the world.

“Step inside and you’ll feel as though you’ve walked straight into Diagon Alley.

“Every detail has been designed to transport fans into the wizarding world. Whether you’re local to London or visiting from afar, we can’t wait to welcome fans through our doors this November.”

The shop will join the collection of Harry Potter experiences owned and operated by Warner Bros in London including Warner Bros Studio Tour London–The Making of Harry Potter and the Harry Potter shop at King’s Cross.

Oxford Street is one of the world’s busiest shopping areas, with around half a million visitors each day.

News.content:

Jaguar has opened the doors of its new all-electric Type 01, giving us our first proper look at the radical interior before the whole car is unveiled in New York on 6 October.

I’ve already been allowed inside, and first impressions are of a stunning, high-quality cabin that sticks closely to Jaguar’s “copy nothing” mantra. The layout is clean and simple, the materials feel suitably special and the Jaguar branding is subtle rather than shouted from every surface.

The biggest surprise is what isn’t there. The Type 01 has no rear window, so there’s no conventional rear-view mirror either. Cameras take care of the view behind, feeding a digital display positioned much farther forward at the base of the windscreen and at the same height as the door mirrors.

open image in gallery The Jaguar Type 01 features minimalist seats front and rear, a strong brass-trimmed centre spine, a long panoramic glass roof and no rear screen ( Jaguar )

That location makes it easier to glance at than a screen hanging in the usual mirror position, although the absence of a proper mirror is still likely to divide opinion.

Look up and there’s a wonderful full-length panoramic glass roof. It stretches as far back as possible over the heads of those in the rear, with only the need for a roof aerial interrupting the view at the back.

Running through the middle of the cabin is a huge central spine, which looks chunky enough to support the entire weight of the car. It also makes this strictly a four-seater, creating a separate space for each person, although there appears to be plenty of room for rear passengers.

The spine gives the cabin a strong front-to-back theme, too, rather than the more usual, broad, horizontal dashboards found in so many electric cars.

From the driver’s seat, the Type 01 feels spacious without leaving you isolated from the car. The low driving position is comfortable, while the minimalist seats may look simple, but feel supportive. A slim main screen is clear and easy to read, with a second display offering useful shortcut keys that are likely to be hidden until you need them.

Jaguar says the cabin takes inspiration from travertine stone and handmade textiles. A brass finish runs along that central spine and is repeated across the tops of the doors, where discreet Jaguar leaper badges sit among some unusual textures and more hidden technology.

open image in gallery This overhead shot of the Jaguar Type 01 shows how the strikethrough motif runs from the bonnet through to the dashboard ( Jaguar )

There are concealed storage areas and flashes of colour, while the dashboard and bonnet are designed to look as if they flow into one another with Jaguar’s strikethrough motif carried from bonnet to dash. It’s dramatic, but the cabin doesn’t feel fussy and it’s certainly not overloaded with screens.

Chief interior designer, Thomas Holden, said: “Our holistic design philosophy translates the vehicle’s exterior presence into a distinctive interior architecture. In contrast to the horizontal interior design norm, we emphasise its dramatic longitudinal nature through the central spine – an architectural statement that creates four individual spaces. With authentic materials, technology on demand and reductive flowing surfaces, Type 01 presents unmistakable drama and theatre that will define the modern luxury automotive interior of the future.”

The Type 01 will be a luxury four-door GT and the first production Jaguar to use the brand’s dedicated electric car platform. It has been designed, developed and will be built in the UK. The “Type” name nods to Jaguar’s past, with “0” standing for zero tailpipe emissions and “1” marking the first of a new generation.

open image in gallery The new Jaguar leaper features subtly inset into brass on the top of the Type 01's doors ( Jaguar )

Jaguar managing director Rawdon Glover said: “Jaguar Type 01 is the first production car to follow our new creative philosophy. Unmistakable from every angle, the interior is no different. With Type 01, we wanted every journey to be an occasion, from how it drives to how it looks and how it makes you feel. With a confidence-inspiring GT driving position, clean and sophisticated technology and dramatic styling, Type 01 has an interior like no other.”

A Type 01 prototype will make its North American debut in a new wrap during Monterey Car Week, ending with an appearance at the Pebble Beach Concours on 16 August. The full reveal of the car will be at a lavish event set for 6 October in New York City.

Thousands of pupils newly entitled to free dinners from next month risk missing out because their parents are unaware of the change, a charity has warned.

The Child Poverty Action Group (Cpag) has urged the Government to do more to ensure families are informed about the policy shift.

Originally announced last June, the widened criteria take effect in September and are expected to make over half a million additional pupils eligible for Free School Meals (FSMs).

The reform means all households claiming universal credit (UC), above the existing £7,400 cap, will qualify.

According to previous statements from the Government, the change could save families up to £495 a year per child on lunch costs.

The expansion is projected by the Government to lift around 100,000 children out of poverty before the end of this Parliament.

However, Cpag research indicates that more than half of affected parents do not realise their children qualify, raising concerns that the support will go underused at a critical time for families.

Cpag’s small survey, carried out online by pollster Survation between June and early August, found that of the 201 parents in England on UC credit whose children are currently ineligible but will qualify from next month, 55% were unaware they will be affected by the change.

Cpag research indicates that more than half of affected parents do not realise their children qualify for free school meals ( PA )

The charity said it should be the Government, rather than “hard-pressed schools and local authorities”, identifying and informing newly eligible families, insisting that departments have the “data and the means of informing parents and must utilise these to make sure that all eligible parents know that they qualify and know what they need to do to register”.

Cpag’s head of education policy Kate Anstey said: “Our survey shows wider eligibility for free school meals will give hard-up families some badly-needed breathing space.

“But September is only weeks away and our new analysis shows the DWP (Department for Work and Pensions) and DfE (Department for Education) have left the job half done. With so many families struggling, it’s on Government to ensure the country’s children get what little help is available.”

Paul Whiteman, general secretary at school leaders’ union NAHT, said the policy change is “enormously welcome” but that “checking eligibility will create additional barriers and unnecessary workload for schools”.

He said: “We urge the DWP and DfE to use the records at their disposal to directly inform newly eligible families.

“This would ensure they and their children benefit as soon as possible while alleviating the burden on schools and parents.

“This situation could be avoided entirely through the introduction of auto-enrolment for free school meals, something NAHT has long called for.”

A Department for Education spokesperson said: “Families up and down the country are feeling the pressure of the cost of living. That’s why this Government is proud to give free school meals to every child from a household on universal credit, alongside expanding childcare and rolling out free breakfast clubs across the country.

“This is a historic step, backed by over £1 billion, and it means 500,000 more children will benefit.

“We’re working closely with schools and councils to make sure every eligible family knows about it. So if you’re a parent and you’re not sure whether your child qualifies – just ask the school.”

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football 2026/27: Everything you need to know and FAQs
News.content:
What’s new for 2026/27?





You’ll need to re-register

When signing up to Telegraph Fantasy Football this season you will notice your old logins do not work.

New for this season you will need to register or login to an existing telegraph.co.uk account to play.

NOTE: you do not need to subscribe in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football - it is free to play.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



We’ve had a makeover and Leagues have moved

Over the summer we changed game provider meaning the site was built again from scratch. We hope you like the new look and feel.

We know nobody likes change, but take your time to get to know the new layout as some aspects of the site may have moved slightly.

The most notable change is that Leagues are now created and joined below your team selection.



Back to basics

With such a short space of time to get the TFF live for this season, the game has been stripped back to basics.

You’ll notice there are no Public Leagues and no prizes for Weekly and Monthly Leaderboard winners. Assistant Manager has also not been integrated for launch.



The Fixture Tracker

Whilst the game has been stripped back to basics, you’ll notice a new fixture tracker above your team selection. This is there to help you make transfer decisions and we hope you like it.



No rule changes.

Whilst some things may have changed, the rules remain unchanged.

Telegraph Fantasy Football is fantasy football at its purest. No gimmicks, no boosts, no captains. Simply pick the best XI players you can.



Assists

However, this season assists will no longer follow Opta’s “Fantasy Assist” definition and revert back to standard assists.



Did you miss it? League Cup fixtures and five more transfers

In case you missed it last year, this season will also feature League Cup fixtures meaning all competitive domestic football containing Premier League fixtures will count towards your Telegraph Fantasy Football points tally.

Why the change? Well for years the general advice early in the season is to hold onto your transfers and we thought that was getting a bit stale. With League Cup fixtures starting as early as Game Week 3 some seasons, you’d be a fool not to take advantage of some fixture gains against lower-league opposition.

To help with the additional fixtures we have also added five more transfers to your season total.



Paid leagues are no more

Unfortunately Plucky Paid Leagues are not integrated this season.



Three new teams

Ipswich are no strangers to Telegraph Fantasy Football as they both return from relegations in 2025. They bring with them a host of talent including two big names you might recognise, including Jaden Philogene (£2.9m) and Leif Davis (£2.6m).

It has been a fair few years since Hull City (2016/17) and Coventry City (2000/01) last featured in Telegraph Fantasy Football - memories may even flood back of posting in your transfers for the Sky Blues’ players. Both clubs are favourites to go down, but with some exciting signings like Tzolakis (£2.5m) and Thomas-Asante (£2.7m) they will certainly put up a fight.

Start creating your team >



FAQs





When does Telegraph Fantasy Football start?

The 2026/27 edition of Telegraph Fantasy Football launched on August 10, 2026. The scoring will commence on Friday August 21, 2026 at 8pm when the Premier League champions Arsenal host Coventry.



How do I register for Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You will need to create a new, or use your existing telegraph.co.uk account in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football. Simply click “SIGN UP”, then “Continue with Telegraph” and you will be temporarily taken to telegraph.co.uk to login with your existing Telegraph account or create a new account, before automatically returning back to the Telegraph Fantasy Football site.

Note: this account is not the same as your account from previous Telegraph Fantasy Football seasons.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.

How much does it cost to play Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Telegraph Fantasy Football is completely free to play. All managers compete for the £5,000 prize pool as well the chance to challenge friends, family, colleagues and fellow managers in private mini-leagues.



How many players can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You only have to pick a squad of XI players in Telegraph Fantasy Football. With no bench to rely on, finding players who get minutes on the pitch is key and we help you out there by allowing transfers right up until every kick-off.



How many teams can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can create up to five teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football with a budget of £50m for each, meaning you have a better chance of being in contention for the prizes come the end of the season if some of your selections prove to be unsuccessful.



How many transfers can I make in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Up until the first game on Friday August 21, 2025, there is a transfer amnesty, meaning you can make as many changes as you like. After the season has started you have 45 transfers for the whole campaign with a maximum of five per Game Week (00:00 Tuesday to 23:59 Monday).





How do I join a private league in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Leagues have now moved below your team selection.

This should make it easier for managers to see which league the team is in that they are making changes to.

To join a league click “Join a league” and then add the 6 digit code that the League Chairman will have access to.

To create a league click “Create a league”, name the league and then copy the league code generated to share with your fellow managers.

League Chairmen will have the ability to lock and unlock a league to new joiners.



Do ALL Cup games count in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Yes. All League Cup fixtures plus all FA Cup games involving Premier League sides count towards your TFF points tally. This adds a great dimension to the game as you will want to load your teams with players who make the latter stages for an advantage over your competitors. However, one thing to note is that penalty shoot-outs do not count towards your score.



How many players are in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can expect to compete against more than 100,000 other teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football – a vast but tight-knit community of players where you have every chance of winning one of our many prizes on offer throughout the year.

We aim to include every player in a squad who has a chance of getting some game time. From time to time we may miss a youngster on debut, but rest assured they will soon be added to the player list and feel free to let us know on Facebook or Twitter if you feel someone is missing.

Having technical issues with TFF? Check our Troubleshooting page for help.



What else do I need to know?



Get your strategy right. Getting the balance of your team right can be a tricky business, especially with limited funds, but there are a few tried and trusted methods that will stand you in good stead:



Pick regular starters

Okay, so this isn’t always straightforward in the world of squad rotation where world-class players routinely find themselves sitting on the bench. That said, there are certain players who, if fit, are almost always the first name on the team sheet. Think Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, Jordan Pickford for Everton and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.



Find a couple of budget ‘gems’

Igor Thiago, Nico O’Reilly and James Garner were among a crop of players who began last term in the ‘unfancied’ category and were must-have ‘enablers’ by the time the season was over. If you’re able to identify one or two of this type of player early in the season, you could be on to a winner.



Be transfer savvy

We’ve all been there – you spend hours selecting your team for the big kick-off then half of them don’t start, the other half have stinkers and your star striker gets a season-ending injury. If you do get off to a slow start, don’t panic. Lurching from one strategy to another could do more harm than good, wasting precious transfers in the process. Trust your instincts, tweak where necessary and the points will come.



Read our weekly Selection Guide

The best advice comes from experts at the Fantasy Football Hub who make our weekly selection guide a prolific source of Telegraph Fantasy Football tips and Telegraph Fantasy Football match facts.

If you subscribe to the weekly newsletter this will hit your inbox on Friday around lunchtime; alternatively it can be found on our social channels or Telegraph Fantasy Football content hub.



Telegraph Fantasy Football Player List

We aim to keep our player list up to date with all comings and goings in the transfer window and the first place to look is our trusted Stats Centre. However, if you fancy yourself as a bit of a Telegraph Fantasy Football expert like the team at Fantasy Football Hub, you can find a player list below in a spreadsheet format so you can do your own analysis.

On the document simply click “file”, then “make a copy” and you will have your own version of the player list at that time to edit as you please.



Download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App

Never miss a chance to make a transfer and download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App which is available on iOS and Android.





You can follow the latest Telegraph Fantasy Football news and discussions throughout the year on Facebook, Twitter and Fantasy Football Content Hub.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: transfers explained and top transfer tips
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.



Transfers explained



A good place to start is by explaining the Telegraph Fantasy Football rules on transfers. First thing to note is the pre-season transfer amnesty, so you can make unlimited changes to your teams right up until the first scheduled kick-off on Friday 21 August, 20:00.

45 is the magic number of transfers you receive during the season, five more than last season to help negotiate the new League Cup fixtures. This equates to a little more than one a week. You can use a maximum of five transfers in any Game Week which run from 00:00 on Tuesdays to 23:59 on Mondays.

Four seasons ago we scrapped the two-hour rule, meaning you can make transfers right up until a game kicks off. However, we don’t suggest you leave it that late as if a transfer is not completed in time you will not gain any points for the game from the player transferred in. Starting XIs are released an hour before kick-off so you have an ample window to implement any changes.

Scrapping the two-hour rule also means that this year you can be more flexible with your transfers each week. Once a player’s game has started you will amass their points for the entire game and are free to transfer them out for another player who may be kicking off while the previous game is being played, thus benefiting from two players’ points.



Top transfer strategy tips



1) Utilise fixture gains



Telegraph Fantasy Football is unique amongst other fantasy games in that you can transfer a player out as soon as they’ve played for a player yet to play that day or match week. So if Haaland (£8.3m) played in the 12.30pm Saturday kick-off, managers can transfer him out for Saka (£6.0m) who plays in the 3pm kick-off, and score points for both. Picking up extra fixtures each time a transfer is made is key to TFF success.



2) Find enablers early and stick



To fit in a combination of Erling Haaland (£8.3m), Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m) and Cole Palmer (£6.2m) or similar, requires TFF managers to find cheaper players to balance teams. Finding those players early into the season, and sticking with them to utilise transfers on the other strategy tips, can ensure avoiding wasting transfers on constant restructuring of squads.



3) FA Cup and League Cup (new for 2025/26)

Players in TFF gain points for the League Cup and FA Cup as well as the Premier League, so often players topping points charts at the season end have progressed far in the competition. When seeing lineups for early League Cup and FA Cup Rounds, if big hitting players who are regulars in the league start against lowly opposition, it’s a prime opportunity to stock up on those assets.

New for this season League Cup fixtures have been included which will make the early stages of the season even more exciting when Premier League teams who are not competing in Europe will gain a fixture against the rest.



4) Favourable fixture runs

Picking players who are playing against weaker opposition often score more points, therefore keeping an eye on the fixtures for teams is important.



5) Balance transfers out over the season

There are ~37 gameweeks in the season, so averaging around one transfer a week is a rule of thumb that keeps managers from running out early. The start of the season is the only time your team is reset, so it’s important to set a structure that works for you so that you don’t need to use too many moves at the start to identify those players who are likely to shine. It’s a marathon, not a sprint, so keeping pace early isn’t a necessity, and often keeping a few extra back until the end run sees TFF managers get a late boost.



Pick your free Telegraph Fantasy Football team now >

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football points: a complete guide to scoring
News.content:
How many points for a Goal?

A regular source of goals is often the first thing a manager looks for in a fantasy football team. The highly-priced Erling Haaland is a go-to signing for many, but last season saw the continuation of mid-priced forwards getting in on the action too with the likes of Igor Thiago racking up 22 goals in Telegraph Fantasy Football.

Players get five points per goal scored which, added to starting appearance points (two), mean a regularly starting goal scorer can be a huge asset.



How many points for an Assist?

It won’t take a master tactician to work out that players who rank highly in the goalscoring charts often also feature in the upper echelons of the Assists table.

Bruno Fernandes was head and shoulders above the rest with regard to assist points last season with 21 in total (nine clear of his closest rival).

An assist will earn three points.





What counts as an Assist?

An Assist is the final touch (pass, pass-cum-shot or any other touch) leading to the recipient of the ball scoring a goal.

Outside of fantasy football, if the final touch is deflected by an opposition player, the initiator is only given a goal assist if the receiving player was likely to receive the ball without the deflection having taken place. Own goals, directly taken free kicks, direct corner goals and penalties do not get an assist awarded.

In a change to previous years, Fantasy Assists are not being used.



How many points for a Tackle?

A slightly more nuanced aspect of scoring is the points a player earns for a successful tackle. Managers will need to cast their nets wide to capitalise on tackling points as the highest scorers tend to come from mid-table and even lower-table teams.

Everton’s James Garner was a key beneficiary of tackle bonus points last season with 120 tackles in total. His closest rivals have been very popular this summer with Wolves’ Joao Gomes, now at Aston Villa, and Nottingham Forest’s Elliot Anderson, now at Manchester City. It’s clear from this that deeper lying midfielders are more likely to amass points here.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made during a match and only midfielders are eligible.



What counts as a Tackle?

A tackle is defined as a player connecting with the ball in a ground challenge and successfully taking the ball away from the player in possession. The tackled player must have clearly been in possession of the ball before the tackle was made.

The final destination of the ball (to the tackler, to a teammate, to an opposition player or out of play) is not considered. A tackle will only be deemed unsuccessful if the player tackled retains possession of the ball.

A player cutting out a pass does not count as a tackle.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made.



How many points for a Clean Sheet?

Attainable by goalkeepers and defenders, the top-scorers in the clean sheet category last season mostly came from Arsenal.

There are five clean sheet points on offer for a player who has played at least 60 minutes of a match and two points if the player has played less than an hour where the game has finished with their team conceding zero goals.



How many points for a Save?

In addition to clean sheet points, goalkeepers can earn one point for every two saves made in a match. Much like points for tackling, save points introduce a new angle to team selection with keepers from teams further down the table likely to face more shots than those who generally dominate games. Last season Mark Flekken came out on top with 153 saves for Brentford, so it will be interesting to see how Caoimhin Kelleher gets on this season.



What counts as a Save?



A save is a goalkeeper preventing the ball from entering the goal with any part of his body when facing an intentional attempt to score by an opposition player.

Saves have the following attributes:

Body part: Hands/Feet/Body

Save type: Caught/Collected/Parried Safe/Parried Danger area/Fingertip

Goalkeeper position: Diving/Standing/Reaching/Stooping

For an exhaustive list of how to score Telegraph Fantasy Football points, take a look at our Game Guidelines.

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

Sports.title: Paul Pogba, 33, ‘set to have Monaco contract terminated’ after injury-hit return to football following doping ban
Sports.content:
MONACO are reportedly in talks to terminate Paul Pogba’s contract.

The former Manchester United midfielder, 33, was given the chance to resurrect his career in the Principality last summer after serving a doping ban.



But he has played just 115 minutes of football across six appearances.

And now, according to The Athletic, Pogba and Monaco are thrashing out the terms of a deal that will see them part ways immediately.



Pogba still has a year left to run on his Monaco deal but if the termination goes through he will be free to seek his next club as a free agent.

The 2018 World Cup winner has struggled with fitness and injuries since returning to the professional game last year.



And he suffered a hamstring problem during Monaco’s pre-season tour of England that could now sideline him for several MONTHS.

That is not thought to be the driving force behind the separation talks, however, as negotiations are said to have been rumbling on for several weeks.

Pogba broke down in tears when signing his two-year Monaco deal in 2025.

There was over two years between his final appearance for Juventus and his debut for Monaco, having served part of a four-year doping ban which was reduced to 18 months on appeal by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

Pogba joined United’s academy from Le Havre in 2009 and made seven first-team appearances before joining Juve on a free.

The Frenchman was an instant hit in Italy and re-signed for United in a whopping £89million deal four years later – a world record at the time.

Pogba netted 39 goals in 226 games during an up-and-down second stint with the Red Devils.



He has only played 18 professional matches since leaving Old Trafford in 2022.

Sports.title: Chelsea Files: How The Avengers convinced club legend to join Blues, Xabi Alonso set to cull 40-man squad
Sports.content:
DID you know that The Avengers had a part to play in one of Chelsea’s greatest ever players joining them in 1996?

Apart from it wasn’t Spider-Man, The Hulk and Iron Man convincing Gianluca Vialli to leave Juventus for Stamford Bridge, it was a 1960s TV show with the same name.



Vialli’s move to Chelsea at the time seemed to make no sense.

Juventus had just won the Champions League, with the Blues having just placed 11th in the Premier League, ironically not too dissimilar to where they were last season before spending a bucket-load on Morgan Rogers this summer.



Asked about the move, one of Vialli’s lifelong friends, Luca Dal Monte, exclusively told SunSport about his decision to come to Stamford Bridge.

Dal Monte said: “Gianluca’s decision to join Chelsea was not just a football decision. If you look at it purely in football terms, it made very little sense.

“He was leaving Juventus, who had just won the Champions League, for a Chelsea side that had finished 11th in the Premier League.

“I remember that a few years earlier, when Silvio Berlusconi was making his second attempt to take him to AC Milan, I had actually argued with Gianluca about the importance of winning trophies.

“I remember telling him that a great player becomes truly great not only because of the way he plays or the goals he scores, but also because of the silverware he wins.

“Leaving the Champions of Europe immediately after winning the Champions League seemed almost incomprehensible. But Gianluca felt that his time in Italy had come to an end.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“He had won almost everything there was to win, first with Sampdoria and then with Juventus, and at 32 he wanted something different, not simply another club but another experience of life.

“London had a particular fascination for Italians of our generation. For many of us, it was the destination of our first flight, often for an Easter holiday when we were teenagers.

“Britain had also entered our imagination through television. We had grown up under the spell of British series such as The Avengers – “Mrs Peel, we’re needed!” – and London seemed exciting, stylish and somehow different from anywhere else.

“I think there was also something very characteristic of Gianluca in the decision. He was curious. He was never frightened by change. He could have remained in Italy, where he was famous, successful and completely at home.



“But instead, he chose to put himself in a country where he barely spoke the language and where the football culture was entirely different. In a sense, he chose uncertainty. What he could not possibly have known was how profoundly that decision would change his life.

“Chelsea was supposed to be the next chapter of his career. Instead, it became part of his identity. He arrived as a famous Italian footballer and became a Chelsea man, and Stamford Bridge really did capture his heart.”

Vialli, who arned 59 caps for Italy, tragically died in 2023 at the age of 58 following a six-year battle with cancer.

More of Dal Monte’s tales of his treasured relationship with Vialli can be found in his new biography: The Gentleman: Gianluca Vialli and How He Changed English Football Forever.

MAHD WORLD

MAHDI NICOLL-JAZULI and Reggie Watson looked like the future of Chelsea during the pre-season tour.



But the challenge now is to turn future into present, for them and the rest of the Blues’ impressive crop of youngsters.

MNJ and Watson are still only 16. So although they proved they could mix it in men’s football in Australia and the Far East, and sometimes showed up their more experienced team-mates, loan moves away from Cobham feel unlikely.

The pair’s development may well be best served by “playing up” in PL2 and the Premier League International Cup, competitions for Under-21s, as well as in the Under-18s.

Ryan Kavuma-McQueen, Reggie Walsh and Shim Mheuka are on a different path.

All three have already had a taste of first-team football. Mheuka was also the top goalscorer and player of the season in PL2 last year and surely needs a loan to at least a Championship club, or a top-flight side abroad, in order to take the next step.



Winger Kavuma-McQueen, 17, is being strongly linked with a loan move to Portsmouth. He looks to have the confidence as well as the ability to make an impression in the second tier.

Walsh, also 17 but with a much-improved physique, is now more likely to be able to impose his creative skills, and a spell at League One Wigan is in the offing.

Jesse Derry, who made an eventful first-team debut at the end of the last campaign, has already gone to Sporting Lisbon for the season.

Chelsea have no first-team European football this campaign so much of the hard work for the remainder of the window will involve cutting Xabi Alonso’s squad of around 40 to a more manageable number.

But the club will also be busy finalising plans to make sure the best prospects of the Academy, who also include 17-year-old “Moroccan Messi” Ibrahim Rabbaj, have the best chance of becoming first-team players as soon as possible.



STRAS RELIEF

STRASBOURG fans will doubtless continue their protests against the BlueCo owners they share with Chelsea.

As things stand, Alonso’s first-team squad will contain the former spine of their sister club’s team.

Mike Penders, Mamadou Sarr, Valentin Barco and Emmanuel Emegha are all now in England.



However they perform, Strasbourg fans will feel sore and even more justified in believing their interests and aspirations are being sacrificed for Chelsea’s benefit.

If the quartet are given a chance by Alonso and do well, it will reaffirm the Ligue 1 team’s status as a glorified feeder club.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

If one or more of them barely play for the Blues or are sold or sent out on loan elsewhere, the fans will legitimately question why they were not left in Strasbourg.

Players moving the other way across the English Channel, with goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen set to replace Penders, will do little to appease supporters no matter how well the team does on the pitch.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola agreed to feature in Jose Mourinho’s Netflix doc but backed out after his one condition was not met
Sports.content:
JOSE MOURINHO’S biggest rivals are conspicuous by their absence from his new Netflix documentary.

The three-part series about the former Chelsea and Real Madrid boss has already got football fans talking, with Mourinho revealing a number of fascinating stories from his remarkable career.



One of the biggest revelations is that Mourinho was lined up to replace Sir Alex Ferguson as Manchester United manager before ultimately deciding against it and returning to Chelsea.

The documentary features a host of Mourinho favourites, including John Terry and Frank Lampard as well as the man he was once expected to succeed, Ferguson.



There is even a surprise appearance from Iker Casillas, despite the former Real Madrid goalkeeper being strongly against Mourinho returning to the Spanish giants this summer.

Casillas lost his place as Real Madrid’s No.1 during Mourinho’s reign, with the Portuguese coach hinting that the goalkeeper was leaking dressing-room information to the media.



Their relationship deteriorated, with Casillas’ close friendships with Barcelona players such as Gerard Pique becoming another source of tension.

The fierce rivalry between Real Madrid and Barcelona only added to the drama.

But despite their history, Casillas features in the documentary and is given the chance to tell his side of the story.

So why are some of Mourinho’s biggest rivals missing?

Pep Guardiola



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Perhaps the most surprising omission is Pep Guardiola.

The pair famously developed one of football’s fiercest managerial rivalries during their time in charge of Barcelona and Real Madrid.

But their relationship goes back much further, with Guardiola and Mourinho having worked together at Barcelona.

They later found themselves on opposite sides of Manchester, with Mourinho managing United and Guardiola in charge of City.



Given their history, Guardiola would have been an obvious choice for the documentary.

And SunSport has been told that he was approached.

Guardiola was reportedly open to taking part and sharing his experiences of going head-to-head with Mourinho.

But there was one major condition.

Director Joe Pearlman – the multi-Emmy, Bafta, and Grammy-nominated British documentary maker – told The Sun: “Yes, we did reach out to Pep, who agreed to do an interview but it was on the condition that Jose reached out to him in person.



“You can imagine how that went down.”

Roman Abramovich

Another major absentee is former Chelsea owner Roman Abramovich.



Mourinho first came to widespread English attention when he famously celebrated by running down the Old Trafford touchline after Porto knocked Manchester United out of the Champions League.

That performance is widely regarded as one of the moments that convinced Abramovich he wanted the feisty Portuguese at Chelsea.

Mourinho would go on to become one of the most successful managers in the club’s history, winning two Premier League titles during his first spell at Stamford Bridge.

Yet Abramovich does not feature in the documentary.

SunSport asked Pearlman why they did not pursue an interview with the former Chelsea owner.



He said: “Mr Abramovich has a lot of interviews he should probably do before he talks about his tenure at Chelsea, so no, it wasn’t something we pursued, especially as Peter Kenyon gives the exact same account.”

Arsene Wenger

Then there is Arsene Wenger.



The Frenchman and Mourinho had one of the most entertaining managerial feuds in Premier League history.

Their rivalry produced plenty of memorable moments, with Mourinho famously branding Wenger a “specialist in failure”.

So why was Wenger not interviewed?

Pearlman admits the documentary makers simply did not pursue him.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said: “Wenger says it all in the press conferences, but the honest truth is that we just did not bother reaching out to him.”



While Mourinho’s career has provided plenty of drama, it seems some of the biggest names from his story were either unwilling or simply not approached for the final cut.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez get married in ‘intimate and private ceremony’ as footie legend posts ring
Sports.content:
CRISTIANO RONALDO and Georgina Rodriguez have finally tied the knot.

The pair dropped the bombshell in a joint-Instagram post on Tuesday evening which flaunted their matching gold rings.



It was captioned “C❤️G” and surpassed a million likes in a matter of minutes.

The civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, was described as ‘private and intimate’ by the Daily Mail.



The pair’s five children – two of whom are biologically Georgina’s – were all in attendance.

One of the football star’s representatives told the Mail: “Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez were married today in a civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, and are now officially husband and wife.



“The ceremony was a private and intimate moment attended by their five children.”

The comments section on their Instagram post was chock-full of adoring fans.

One wrote: “We love you guys.”

Another joked: “Who is cutting onions?”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And a third chimed in with: “Wishing you both a happy life together.”

A year on from their engagement, there were rumblings in recent weeks of Georgina, 32, and Ronaldo, 41, finally scheduling their big day.

Thousands of fans gathered outside a cathedral in Funchal over the weekend, on Ronaldo’s home island of Madeira, hoping to catch a glimpse of the couple.

But the newlyweds instead opted for the chic coastal town of Cascais, around 20 miles west of Lisbon.



Ronaldo and Georgina’s marriage was a decade in the making, having met at a Gucci shop in Madrid in 2016.

Georgina was earning £10 an hour as an employee there at the time – and being whisked off in Ronaldo’s Bugatti after work.

They went public with their relationship in 2017, welcomed twins Mateo and Eva via surrogacy later that year, and then Georgina gave birth to her first biological daughter, Alana Martina, who is now eight years old.

In 2022 they welcomed Bella Esmeralda to the family but her twin brother, Angel, tragically died during childbirth.

Mateo, Eva, Alana Martina, Bella Esmeralda and Ronaldo’s eldest son, Cristiano Jr, are all brought up under one roof.



Ronaldo popped the question last year and presented Georgina with a whopping great diamond engagement ring.

And the five-time Ballon d’Or winner offered a hint that their wedding would not be a grand show of public affection when discussing their plans.

He revealed: “We plan to do it after the World Cup with the trophy! But she is not the person that likes big parties. She doesn’t like it. She likes private things. So I will respect these decisions.

“One thing that I love, she didn’t care about the ring.

“She asked me if I was honest and I said, ‘I want you and I want to marry you.’ I didn’t cry but I had tears in my eyes.”

Sports.title: Championship supercomputer predicts 2026-27 standings with firm West Ham verdict
Sports.content:
Championship supercomputer predicts 2026-27 standings with firm West Ham verdict

West Ham were disappointed to be relegated to the Championship at the end of last season but a supercomputer has predicted they will make an immediate return to the Premier League

View 2 Images Bowen and West Ham are bidding for an immediate return to the Premier League (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

West Ham have been tipped to bounce straight back to the Premier League at the first time of asking. The Hammers are short-priced favourites to win the title and return to the top flight after the relegation last term.

‌



And now, a supercomputer simulated by Casino Kings has Nuno Espirito Santo's side topping the table ahead of their first game of the season at Burnley on Sunday.

‌



The Clarets are also predicted to go straight back up, finishing as runners-up, while Wolves are tipped to finish just behind in third. The Molineux side are predicted to be joined in the playoffs by Norwich, Sheffield United, Wrexham, Southampton and Birmingham.

‌



And it will be Cesar Peixoto's men who prevail in the playoff final at Wembley, according to the supercomputer.

Carabao Cup fixture chaos as Chelsea embroiled in crazy eight-game domino effect READ MORE :

Newly-promoted Lincoln are predicted to go straight back down to League One, being joined by Blackburn and QPR in the drop zone.

West Ham have retained the services of talisman and skipper Jarrod Bowen for their Championship campaign, despite interest from the Premier League.

‌



It's their first stint in the Championship since 2012, when they beat Blackpool in the playoff final at Wembley to win promotion thanks to a late goal by Ricardo Vaz Te.

But it will be the first time the London Stadium has played host to second-tier football. The Hammers made a winning start to the season on Saturday as they beat Portsmouth 3-1 in the Carabao Cup.

Sports.title: Man Utd have clear transfer priority after Myles Lewis-Skelly offer
Sports.content:
Man Utd have clear transfer priority after Myles Lewis-Skelly offer

Manchester United have been offered Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly but have their eye on another Premier League left-back as their top summer target

View 2 Images Lewis Hall is Manchester United's top left-back target (Image: Kieran McManus/Shutterstock)

Lewis Hall is Manchester United's number one target for the left-back position, despite being offered Myles Lewis-Skelly, it has been claimed.

‌



Michael Carrick's side remain on the lookout for a left sided defender before the summer transfer window closes and Hall has been identified as the one United want. Indeed, according to The Sun, United view the 21-year-old Newcastle United star as the long-term successor to Luke Shaw and are determined to land his signature before the September 1 transfer deadline.

‌



But the Magpies have taken steps to play down speculation surrounding Hall's potential departure to United and are desperate to retain one of their prized assets, having already lost Anthony Gordon, Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali to Barcelona, Newcastle and Tottenham this summer.

‌



Myles Lewis-Skelly has made his preference clear as Man Utd and Chelsea sounded out READ MORE :

Man Utd ready to open talks over £30m transfer in perfect response to double blow READ MORE :

Hall, meanwhile, is understood to be attracted by a switch to Old Trafford and follow a number of his former teammates through the exit door at Newcastle. And his want to quit the Magpies has remained unchanged despite the appointment of new head coach Matthias Jaissle, who took over from Eddie Howe following his surprise exit last month.

United have stepped up their pursuit of Hall, who is under contract until 2029, in recent weeks and are eyeing up him as him their fourth signing of the summer. The Reds have invested more than £80m so far on Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow, and are still targeting a couple more recruits.

View 2 Images Lewis Hall is a key target for Manchester United (Image: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

‌



But United could face a significant challenge to secure Hall given Newcastle's reported £60m asking price. The Reds have rejected the valuations of Premier League trio Mateus Fernandes, Alex Scott and Elliot Anderson, and are unwilling to overpay for any target, irrespective of their identity.

Lewis-Skelly represents another possibility for United after he was made available to Carrick's side earlier this week. The 19-year-old excelled in midfield for Arsenal towards the end of last season but is equally adept at left-back.

The Gunners are looking to raise funds following Bruno Guimaraes' £75m arrival and view Lewis-Skelly as a sellable asset. Alongside United, the Hale End graduate has also been offered to Premier League counterparts Chelsea.

‌



Yet Lewis-Skelly is keen on remaining at Arsenal and United would rather pursue Hall in any case, shelving that transfer speculation firmly aside, at least for the time being.

Hall was sent home from Newcastle's pre-season training camp in La Manga, Spain last week after suffering a minor injury. He consequently missed Jaissle's first game away at Valencia.

Sports.title: Man Utd make decision on top transfer target after Myles Lewis-Skelly U-turn
Sports.content:
Man Utd make decision on top transfer target after Myles Lewis-Skelly U-turn

Manchester United are in the market for another central midfielder and also want to add a left-back but do not appear to be considering a move for Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly

View 2 Images Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly could be on the move (Image: (Photo by Marc Atkins/Getty Images))

Manchester United are set to continue their pursuit of Lewis Hall in their search for a new left-back despite once again being offered the chance to sign Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly.

‌



The Red Devils have prioritised midfielders in the transfer window this summer, completing deals for Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. It's understood the club would like to add another central midfielder before the deadline, however, there are other areas which still need strengthening ahead of the upcoming Premier League campaign.

‌



United would ideally like to add another left-back who has the potential to become Luke Shaw's long-term successor at Old Trafford.

‌



Hall has been a priority target despite doubts over whether Newcastle, having already sanctioned significant sales for Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, would consider doing a deal.

Myles Lewis-Skelly has made his preference clear as Man Utd and Chelsea sounded out READ MORE :

Man Utd ready to open talks over £30m transfer in perfect response to double blow READ MORE :

But United's stance hasn't changed according to The Sun, who claim they have no interest in pursuing a deal for Lewis-Skelly.

The Arsenal midfielder has featured prominently for the Premier League champions at left-back and was previously offered to United via an intermediary back in January. At the time, they were understood to be more receptive to a deal, although they were quoted a price of around £60million for the 19-year-old.

‌



Arsenal have grand ambitions to level up the squad that came within a whisker of a Premier League and Champions League double and player sales will be necessary to facilitate further quality signings. As an academy graduate, any funds raised from selling Lewis-Skelly would equate to pure profit, giving Arsenal greater financial flexibility in the market. Chelsea have also been offered the chance to sign Lewis-Skelly.

View 2 Images Lewis Hall is Manchester United's preferred left-back target (Image: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Hall remains United's priority transfer target and, while Newcastle do not want to lose him, the player is keen on moving to Old Trafford, the report adds.

‌



His desire to pursue a new challenge is likely to represent an early headache for the club's new head coach, Matthias Jaissle, who has replaced Eddie Howe at the helm.

Hall has established himself as one of the top left-back's in the Premier League since joining Newcastle from Chelsea back in 2023. The 21-year-old made 30 appearances in the league for Newcastle last term, scoring one goal.

Sports.title: Rodri has a huge transfer decision to make - he's outgrown Man City and MUST leave
Sports.content:
Rodri has a huge transfer decision to make - he's outgrown Man City and MUST leave

Manchester City midfielder Rodri is wanted by Spain's two biggest clubs and can pretty much take his pick with his future - his decision should be to LEAVE the Premier League

View Image Rodri has proved himself again to be the best midfielder on the planet (Image: 2026 Luciano Lima)

Rodri has the kind of choice to make most footballers can only dream about. And remaining at Manchester City should NOT be one of them.

‌



When Real Madrid and Barcelona come calling at the same time, it speaks volumes for your standing in the game. Two of the biggest clubs on the planet going head-to-head for your services. Which is how it should be, because Rodri is the best midfielder on the planet.

‌



A footballer who has outgrown his current club.

‌



Rodri has nothing left to prove or achieve in the blue half of Manchester. He has won the lot, including a Treble in 2023, having had a crucial role in elevating City to the ultimate level. And with Pep Guardiola having walked into the sunset, it feels like the time is now right for Rodri to seek a fresh challenge at the age of 30.

Ryan Reynolds delivers perfect response to US couple moving from Texas to Wrexham READ MORE :

What Marcus Rashford really thinks about staying at Manchester United this season READ MORE :

The Spaniard is at his peak. He proved this in the summer, leading Spain to World Cup glory.

Having now won the ultimate prize, to sit alongside the Euros triumph of 2024, Ballon d'Or accolade and countless club trophies, there might be little left for Rodri to aim for.

‌



But someone like him should be desperate to add more layers to his legacy. And the place to do this should either be in Barcelona or Madrid.

The Nou Camp and Bernabeu are two genuine cathedrals of football. Fitting stages for the incredible talents Rodri has.

Turning down Real in favour of Barca would not be everyone's choice. When it comes to history, tradition and standing in the game, no-one quite compares to the 15-time Champions League winners. A club the great Guardiola once labelled the "kings of Europe".

‌



But joining Barca, like what Rodri is expected to do in the coming days, would be quite the second prize. The reigning Spanish champions remain a monster of a club.

One the likes of City will never be able to draw comparisons with. One with millions of supporters around the globe. One which has winning the biggest club prizes embedded in its DNA.

Rodri owes City nothing.

‌



He cost them £62.6m from Atletico Madrid, but went on to become a priceless addition to the team's progress. So if and when Rodri decides to say goodbye to the Etihad, supporters should bid him a fond farewell and give him their blessing.

While City bosses should give fans a lasting reminder of how much he contributed. By giving the bloke a statue outside the stadium.

Sports.title: Man Utd 'ready to trigger release clause' and forced to act quick after £20m agreement
Sports.content:
Man Utd 'ready to trigger release clause' and forced to act quick after £20m agreement

Manchester United continue to be linked with a host of names, even though they have added six new faces to Michael Carrick's squad this summer

View 2 Images Michael Carrick could be getting a new left back before the season gets underway (Image: (Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images))

Manchester United are ready to trigger Jorge Salinas’ release clause - but face competition from Atletico Madrid for his signature. Salinas came through the ranks at Real Racing Club de Santander and went on to make his first-team debut back in 2024.

The left-back has since impressed in Spain, and, as a result, has been linked with a move away. As well as Atletico and United, Salinas has also been linked with a move to Barcelona.

However, according to Spanish publication Sport, Barca have no intention of paying Salinas’ €16m (£13.6m) release clause. United, though, are ready to trigger it to snap up the 19-year-old this summer.

But in a twist, the report also claims that Atletico are waiting for Matteo Ruggeri to complete a move to Aston Villa before making a move for Salinas. It is claimed that Villa have agreed a €18m plus €6m bonuses (£20m) deal with Los Rojiblancos for Ruggeri, meaning United may have to act quickly.

Despite the continued speculation around Salinas’ future, Racing boss Jose Alberto Lopez claimed earlier this week that the defender, along with Gustavo Puerta, don’t want to leave the club this summer. He said: "Their professionalism doesn't surprise me.

What Marcus Rashford really thinks about staying at Manchester United this season READ MORE :

Man Utd preparing for four transfer exits as Michael Carrick green lights departures READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UNITED FB PAGE! Latest news and analysis via the MEN’s Manchester United Facebook page

“What surprises me is that people are constantly talking about the departure of two of our players [Salinas and Puerta], when they have contracts and are our players."

Before he added: "They're very important to us. I don't want them to leave. And they show every day that they don't either.

“But we know how this world works and there are release clauses. If a team comes along and pays the clause, they cease to be our players."

View 2 Images Jorge Salinas is a key target with United said to be ready to meet his release clause

Speaking last week, Racing sporting director Chema Aragon made similar comments, but he did admit that his club would be powerless if a 'giant' such as United and Barca came in with a significant bid for Salinas.

"There's little you can do if a giant appears," Aragan said. "We value the assets we have, we consider them important.

“For the club, at this time, there is no other option than to try to strengthen the team and not weaken it by losing stars. The reality is that the club that wants him has to come along with an offer."

United are in the market for a left back and are considering alternatives for Lewis Hall, who Newcastle do not want to sell. Salinas has already represented Spain's under-19 side nine times and registered seven assists from 34 matches last season as Racing were promoted back to La Liga.

Sports.title: Chelsea and Man Utd offered Myles Lewis-Skelly as Arsenal open to shock sale despite new deal
Sports.content:
Manchester United and Chelsea have been offered the opportunity to sign Myles Lewis-Skelly from Arsenal, according to the Mirror's sister-title football.london. The unexpected scenario has arisen following the Gunners' recent signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United for £75million.

Despite only agreeing a new contract last summer, the 19-year-old has been made available to Chelsea as well as Manchester United. It is currently unclear whether or not either Premier League club will formalise a pursuit but there has been strong links to Old Trafford in the last 12 months.

Michael Carrick's side are looking to sign a midfielder and left-back before the summer transfer window closes and Lewis-Skelly, capable of playing in both positions, is arguably the perfect addition.

Audacious Marcus Rashford swap deal proposed with Arsenal star joining Man Utd READ MORE :

An ambitious swap deal could even be sanctioned given Arsenal's need to sign a left winger with Marcus Rashford's future still uncertain. That very scenario has been suggested as a positive for both parties given what Lewis-Skelly and Rashford need going forward.

‌



Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos have already joined to strengthen the engine room with a third signing targeted. Newcastle United's Lewis Hall was their top target at left-back, but unlike Lewis-Skelly, he is not available for sale.

Jorge Salinas of Racing Santander has since emerged as an option but he is favouring a move to Barcelona which could open the door for Lewis-Skelly. United have already poached Ayden Heaven and Chido Obi from Arsenal's academy and Lewis-Skelly could be third to join in only a few years.

From Chelsea's perspective, it is understood that if a lucrative proposal was to be submitted by the Blues, their London rivals would find it difficult to reject it. Lewis-Skelly would be more likely to play in midfield consistently under Xabi Alonso with Jorrel Hato able to play at left-back and Pep Chavarria set to join from Rayo Vallecano following Marc Cucurella's move to Real Madrid.

View 2 Images Myles Lewis-Skelly is familiar with several Chelsea and Manchester United players

‌



Chelsea have already spent big this summer to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa but another big fee for a Premier League star could open the door for Enzo Fernandez to leave with Real Madrid and Manchester City interested.

Lewis-Skelly has started every pre-season fixture as a defensive midfielder with Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Guimaraes all unavailable.

His displays have been inconsistent, despite performing brilliantly in the left eight position towards the end of last season, which earned him a starting berth in the Champions League final.

Sports.title: Paul Scholes begs Man Utd to sign £30m 'absolute idiot' and admits 'you might laugh'
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes begs Man Utd to sign £30m 'absolute idiot' and admits 'you might laugh'

Cristian Romero is set to leave Tottenham this summer and Manchester United legend Paul Scholes has urged his former club to hijack the transfer

View 2 Images Paul Scholes is a fan of Cristian Romero (Image: PA)

Paul Scholes believes Manchester United should try to hijack a move for Cristian Romero, whom he described as an 'absolute idiot.' The Argentine, appointed captain only last year after signing a four‑year deal, is expected to leave Tottenham this summer, with Atletico Madrid currently in negotiations over his transfer.

‌



Fabrizio Romano reports that the deal between Spurs and Atletico is edging closer, though clubs are still a few million apart on the guaranteed fee and have yet to finalise the bonus structure. Atletico remain determined and are preparing a new offer.

‌



Inter Milan, Barcelona and Arsenal have also shown interest, but a sale to Spurs' north London rivals appears highly unlikely. Despite Romero favouring Atleti, Scholes believes United should attempt a late hijack, arguing that adding a top‑level centre‑back alongside Lisandro Martinez and Harry Maguire would be crucial as they prepare for a demanding season across all competitions.

‌



Audacious Marcus Rashford swap deal proposed with Arsenal star joining Man Utd READ MORE :

Man Utd preparing for four transfer exits as Michael Carrick green lights departures READ MORE :

"This is one you might laugh at," Scholes said on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast. "[United should sign] Cristian Romero from Tottenham. I know he's a nutter. I know he's got disciplinary issues.

"But I just think he can be a very good centre-half and I think someone like Michael [Carrick] could really calm him down. And you're talking 30 or 40 million quid. This is a fella who's played centre half and won the World Cup. Now, like I said, I know he's got issues, disciplinary issues."

Scholes added: "There's a bit of something about him. He's won the Europa League with Spurs, he's won a World Cup, two Copa Americas. There's definitely something about him....and he's cheap, £30-40million.

‌



"I think centre-half is probably the biggest [area that needs addressing]. You need to have centre-halves that are reliable for the Premier League. You'd like to have them [fit enough to play] in most games.

View 2 Images Paul Scholes would like to see Romero at Man United

"Harry Maguire not so much, but Martinez picks up a lot of injuries. They've got the young lad Ayden Heaven, who I think is a really bright prospect, but he's still going to make mistakes. He's young. Centre-half is a position they need to address if they are going to be challenging towards the top end [of the league]."

‌



Romero previously came close to leaving Spurs, most notably after Ange Postecoglou's departure. Roberto De Zerbi has since made it clear that he would respect Romero's wish to move on from north London.

"At the beginning of my time, in April, I had, I don't know, one million individual meetings!" he said. "And [the players] told me what was their idea. I said: 'Yes, help me to stay up, and then I help you to leave'. If you don't help me to stay up, you stay underwater with me!"

"But Romero with me was unbelievable. Top. In his behaviour, his respect, he suffered when he did not play the last game. It is not true that he wanted to leave for Argentina to prepare for their World Cup. It's not true."

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

De Zerbi added: "After the semi-final [against England] we text a message, but I never called him to convince him to stay. I respected what he told me. Like for Vicario, like for every player. Romero as a player is one of the best centre-backs in the world, but at the end I said I want to respect the will of the players."

United have already added three new faces to Michael Carrick's squad - Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow. With the window running until 1 September, there's still time for another defensive signing, and Bologna centre‑back Jhon Lucumi is one of the names in the frame.

Article continues below

The Colombia international, who featured at the World Cup, is said to be keen on joining a 'big club' this summer. Bologna want £21.4m (€25m) plus £2.6m (€3m) in bonuses, and United are considering whether to match the asking price.

Sports.title: Arsenal set to receive millions back from Newcastle days after Bruno Guimaraes transfer
Sports.content:
Arsenal set to receive millions back from Newcastle days after Bruno Guimaraes transfer

Arsenal could have Newcastle United to thank for a summer transfer boost days after raiding St James' Park to sign Bruno Guimaraes

View 2 Images Arsenal signed Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United for £75m but could recoup millions (Image: (Photo by David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

Arsenal could be set to recoup some of the £75m transfer fee they paid for Bruno Guimaraes just days later, thanks to a shrewd transfer clause included as part of Joe Willock's switch to Newcastle United. The Gunners negotiated a sell-on clause with the Magpies when Willock moved to St. James' Park back in 2021.

‌



The 26-year-old left the Emirates Stadium in a deal valued at £25million after an impressive loan spell with the Magpies, but his five-year stay in the North East may be coming to an end. Willock is now believed to be close to a £17.4m move to Turkish Super Lig outfit Besiktas, with Newcastle having turned down a £10m bid earlier this summer.

‌



Our sister title ChronicleLive reports Willock's representatives have travelled to Turkey to negotiate a move with Besiktas, reportedly reaching agreement on personal terms. The former Arsenal midfielder is entering the final 12 months of his contract at St. James' Park and Newcastle are keen to recoup a fee.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting READ MORE :

That's positive news for the Gunners, who secured a sell-on clause rumoured to be around 20 per cent, though the precise percentage remains undisclosed. Arsenal spent £75m to take Guimaraes to north London and could bank millions from Willock's prospective move, recouping some of the money paid for the Brazilian.

Gunners fans got a first glimpse of the new midfield addition ahead of the Emirates Cup clash with Borussia Dortmund at the weekend. As for his former Magpies teammate, Willock has featured 168 times for Newcastle, netting 11 goals since his departure from the Gunners.

‌



He broke into the Arsenal first team in 2017 and memorably scored on his Premier League debut against Newcastle in April 2018. Willock racked up 78 appearances and registered 11 goals during four campaigns at the club.

View 2 Images Willock found a new home in the north east (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

The clause now ensures Mikel Arteta's side will profit financially. Arsenal are looking to bolster their squad ahead of their Premier League title defence, having already brought in Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapie, Illan Meslier and Guimaraes.

‌



The additional funds will provide a welcome boost in their bid to secure further signings this summer, with the Gunners actively seeking a new left-winger.

Arsenal had been linked with moves for Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior, however Chelsea swooped in to snap up the England international, while Real Madrid tied down the Brazilian star to fresh terms.

Sports.title: Jets' Stiggers in hospital after collapsing during practice
Sports.content:
New York Jets cornerback Qwan'tez Stiggers collapsed during a joint practice with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers; Stiggers regained consciousness and was talking on the field before being taken to hospital; Jets head coach Aaron Glenn later gave a positive update on Stiggers' condition

New York Jets cornerback Qwan'tez Stiggers was taken to a hospital by ambulance after he briefly lost consciousness during a joint practice with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Tuesday.

Jets coach Aaron Glenn said the 24-year-old was conscious and talking on the field before being put on a stretcher and taken for further examination. There was no immediate word on Stiggers' condition, but Glenn indicated the cornerback was doing okay.

"He was able to talk and I want to make sure I go and see him after this, just to make sure I'm good with everything," Glenn said. "But for the most part, he was good."

The Jets and Buccaneers were in the middle of special-teams drills when Glenn said Stiggers came to the sideline.

"He actually fell out," Glenn said. "The good thing is, he was conscious. Our guys did a hell of a job, just like most medical staffs around this league do in situations like that, and they took the necessary steps just to make sure that we do everything we can to be on board when it comes to those situations."

It was a somewhat scary scene, though, as several Jets team-mates took a knee near the sideline and some formed a prayer circle.

After several minutes, Stiggers was placed on a stretcher with what appeared to be an IV and loaded into the ambulance as fans seated near the area clapped in support.

"It was very sad, very emotional," Jets running back Breece Hall said. "You get on your knee and say a prayer for him and hope he's okay."

Defensive tackle Harrison Phillips added: "What's been shared to us is things are on the up and up."

Practice resumed after being halted for more than 10 minutes while Stiggers was being attended to.

Stiggers was earlier involved in one of the handful of chippy moments during the practice when he had his helmet flung down the field by a Buccaneers player after players on both teams scuffled.

Stiggers is entering his third season with the Jets after being a fifth-round draft pick in 2024. He was one of that draft's feelgood stories because he had no college football experience and was the first player drafted directly from the CFL, where he played for the Toronto Argonauts, since Miami took Jermaine Haley in 1999.

In 29 games, including five starts, with New York, Stiggers has 35 tackles, two fumble recoveries and three passes defended. He is also one of the Jets' top special teams players.

Sports.title: Super Giants rout SunRisers to move to cusp of Hundred eliminator
Sports.content:
Manchester Super Giants routed SunRisers Leeds to all but seal their place in The Hundred men's eliminator and leave their opponents at risk of being knocked out.

The Super Giants restricted SunRisers to 127 all out from their 100 balls as England's Gus Atkinson (3-30) and Sonny Baker (2-22) led the way, before opening batters Tim Seifert (80no from 40) and Paul Walter (44no from 28) knocked off the target with 33 balls to spare.

The huge margin of victory saw the Super Giants move above SunRisers into second place in the group table, with both sides on 20 points but Manchester having edged ahead on net run-rate. The result also confirmed Trent Rockets' place in Sunday's final as table-toppers.

Super Giants and SunRisers occupy the positions that would see them meet in Friday's eliminator for a place in the final, but can still technically be caught by fourth-placed MI London and fifth-placed Welsh Fire, who go into their final group-stage matches on Wednesday on 16 points, meaning wins would take them to 20 points.

While Welsh Fire's negative net run-rate of -1.001 makes it almost impossible they could catch either Super Giants or SunRisers when they face London Spirit, a big win for MI London away to Birmingham Phoenix could feasibly lift them into second or third.

Welsh Fire's clash with London Spirit is live on Sky Sports from 3pm, with MI London's trip to Edgbaston following at 6.30pm.

Asked whether he knew the net run-rate permutations ahead of the chase, Seifert, the Match Hero, said: "I had no idea, to be honest. A message got run out when we needed about 50 runs and that's when we looked to put the pedal down.

"We've got a great side and it's a great environment to play in. It's my first time playing in The Hundred and it's a great tournament to be involved in. It's great to be playing in front of good crowds in amazing stadiums."
