Seifert bludgeoned his third fifty in as many knocks and struck seven sixes, while Walter thumped three maximums of his own as the SunRisers' attack was put to the sword.

The Super Giants' opening pair were electric but the foundations for a stunning win were laid by their bowlers, who clawed things back after Ryan Rickelton and Mitchell Marsh had made a rapid start for the visitors, posting 42 from 22 balls before Rickelton became the first of Atkinson's three victims.

Marsh (32 from 23), the tournament's leading run-scorer, continued his fine form, but when he was snaffled at extra cover off Noor Ahmad, the visitors lost their way.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A spectator was caught knitting at The Hundred!

Harry Brook, Dan Lawrence and Matthew Revis all fell cheaply and when Zak Crawley's stuttering innings of 31 from 28 was ended by Baker, the wheels came off.

SunRisers could only muster 14 runs from the final 14 balls of the innings, for the loss of four wickets. Expensive earlier in the piece, Atkinson was exceptional, taking two wickets and conceding just three runs from the final five.

Sports.title: SunRisers beat Super Giants to reach Hundred eliminator
Sports.content:
Reigning champions SunRisers Leeds snatched a spot in the women's Hundred eliminator by beating Manchester Super Giants by 41 runs in a winner-takes-all game at Old Trafford.

In a shoot-out for the final place in the top three, Annabel Sutherland's unbeaten 62 off 36 balls helped Leeds leapfrog their opponents and set up an eliminator clash against Southern Brave.

The Australian all-rounder hit nine boundaries, including three sixes, as the visitors posted 166-4 after being put in to bat.

Visiting spinner Jess Jonassen took 3-21, while Deepti Sharma and Sutherland claimed two wickets apiece, as Manchester were restricted to 125-8 in reply and exited the competition after slipping to fourth place in the standings.

Second-placed Leeds will continue their title defence against Southern Brave on Friday at The Oval, with table-topping Trent Rockets awaiting the winner in Sunday's final at Lord's.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player UNBELIEVABLE athletic fielding from SunRisers' Phoebe Litchfield to prevent a six

Sutherland, the Match Hero, said: "It's the beauty of being an all-rounder, you're in the game all the time, and I love competing, especially in a match we were calling a final. We had to win and it was nice to do a job for the team."

Phoebe Litchfield made her intentions clear after SunRisers were asked to bat, the Aussie opener racing to 27 from 12 deliveries to leapfrog Sophia Dunkley at the top of the competition's run-scoring chart.

An electrifying innings was brought to a halt after Litchfield miscued a drag down from Mady Villiers but Bryony Smith (17 off 16) and Lauren Winfield-Hill (20 off 15) kept the scoreboard ticking.

When Gibson fell to Villiers with 12 balls remaining, SunRisers were handily placed on 119-4, and Sutherland propelled the visitors to 166-4 - the highest score in the women's competition at Emirates Old Trafford - carting the unfortunate Ryana MacDonald-Gay for three consecutive sixes to round off the innings.

Sports.title: Levy goes up against Spurs owners to buy London's NBA Europe team
Sports.content:
Former Tottenham chairman Daniel Levy is vying with a consortium including current Spurs' owners, the Lewis family, to buy NBA Europe's London-based team.

Sky News has revealed that the Lewises are part of a consortium, led by the Checketts family, which has submitted an offer as part of the ongoing auction.

The Checketts have owned or invested in professional sports franchises including Major League Soccer team Real Salt Lake and the NHL's St Louis Blues.

The third leg of the consortium is the Eccles family, who own shares in Burnley FC and Spanish side Espanyol along with the Checketts.

Sky News has previously reported Levy's involvement in a consortium including Liberty Global and MSP Sports Capital, a former backer of McLaren Racing, which is also among the contenders for the NBA London team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kaveh Solhekol examines where Daniel Levy was 'pushed' out of his role as Spurs chairman

London has rapidly become most highly prized of the 12 new NBA Europe outfits, with other teams based in cities such as Berlin, Manchester, Milan, Munich, Paris and Rome.

The NBA wants to generate billions of dollars by selling the rights to the teams, with the first transactions expected in the coming weeks.

Wealthy US families and investors are increasingly buying stakes in sports teams in the UK, especially in football.

Levy left his role as Spurs executive chairman in September 2025 after nearly 25 years in the job.

While the official communication from Spurs and Levy was that he had "stepped down" from the role, it was widely understood that the decision was taken out of his hands.

Sports.title: Floodlights to be on throughout Hundred matches for solar eclipse
Sports.content:
Floodlights will be turned on throughout games in The Hundred on Wednesday due to the solar eclipse.

Up to 90 per cent of the sun will be obscured by the moon during the eclipse, which will occur between 6.17pm and 8.06pm, peaking shortly after 7pm.

It will be the first partial solar eclipse for 27 years and will be visible across Europe, with some places experiencing a total eclipse, where the sun, moon and earth all line up in space.

The light will dim, the temperature will drop and the wind may change direction as the sun disappears behind the moon. After a few minutes the sun will reappear and daylight will return.

There are four games in The Hundred taking place on Wednesday, all of them live on Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Seifert & Walter hit 10 HUGE sixes in Super Giants win

Welsh Fire women face London Spirit women at 11.30am in Cardiff, followed by the men's game at 3pm. Birmingham Phoenix women host MI London at Edgbaston from 3pm before the men's teams play each other at 6.30pm.

In anticipation for the solar eclipse, organisers will keep floodlights on throughout all four matches and additional messaging will be issued to fans.

Experts have warned that only special solar eclipse glasses that are certified for the safest eye protection should be used to view the eclipse.

Floodlights will be on 'plenty early' at Kempton

Kempton is all set to stage racing on Wednesday during the solar eclipse.

While the twilight meeting at Ffos Las will begin and end earlier than originally scheduled to ensure all six races take place in daylight, there are no such issues at Kempton due to the floodlights that are in place at the Sunbury circuit.

Image: The floodlights will also be turned on at Kempton race course

The eclipse is expected to occur between 7.02pm and 7.16pm and Kempton has races scheduled to take place at 7pm and 7.30pm.

Kempton's clerk of the course Barney Clifford said: "The last one was nearly 30 years ago so I wasn't quite at Kempton then. I remember it but there were no floodlights in those days!

"I'm going to put the floodlights on early doors. I know they have predicted a time for it but you don't quite know how much of the sun is going to be covered and for what race so we'll have the lights on plenty early enough."

Sports.title: Inter Milan in talks over Spurs and England defender Spence
Sports.content:
Tottenham are in talks with Inter Milan over the sale of Djed Spence.

Inter believe a total package of £30m could be enough to get a deal done and Spurs are understood to be willing to sell if they receive an acceptable offer.

Spence's opportunities could be limited at Spurs this season with Destiny Udogie and Andy Robertson also competing for the left-back position and the ever-present Pedro Porro the clear first choice on the right.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After Spence's brilliant cameo off the bench against Norway, England fans Ben Cipolla and Dan Lucas came up with a new song for the full-back titled 'Total Eclipse of Djed Spence'

Inter want to bring in a new player who can operate as a wing-back.

Spence has been high on their list all summer and Inter are now turning their attention to the Spurs man after struggling to strike a deal for Al Ittihad's Moussa Diaby.

De Zerbi: Spurs aren't done in the transfer window

Roberto de Zerbi maintains Tottenham are "not finished yet" in the transfer market as they look to build a competitive Premier League squad again.

Having only avoided relegation on the final day of last season, Spurs have spent already spent around £237m - with the club's transfer record broken twice in deals for Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tottenham Hotspur head coach Roberto De Zerbi tells the Men in Blazers Network that he expects to make more signings this summer (Pictures: Men in Blazers Network)

Dutch defender Jan Paul van Hecke also arrived from Brighton for £52m, while Martin Dubravka, Robertson and Marcos Senesi signed on as free agents.

With Micky van de Ven having also committed his long-term future to the club, there is genuine hope Spurs will soon be challenging at the other end of the table.

"In the transfer market, we have not finished yet [with] the players who will arrive," De Zerbi said, speaking to the Men in Blazers Network.

"We are looking forward to start another season with, I don't know [different] ambitions, but with different results."

De Zerbi continued: "The club has been great because they closed [deals for] very, very important players. I think we have not finished yet.

"Okay, we spent money, but the other clubs made the same or more in the past. To compete in the Premier League, you need first [the] level of the players.

"The ambition of the owner of the club, of the board, of the people who decide behind me are very important and very high, so we have to find the condition to build a strong team, a stronger team than the last seasons, to compete again for the top of the table."

Sports.title: Unbeaten star Bow Echo in shock retirement after setback
Sports.content:
Bow Echo has been retired from racing after the shock news that George Boughey's unbeaten star has suffered a setback in training.

Having won the 2000 Guineas, the St James's Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot and the Sussex Stakes this season, Bow Echo was being lined up for Sunday's Prix Jacques le Marois.

Announcing the surprise news on his X account, Boughey said: "It is with great disappointment that we have to announce that Bow Echo has had a setback and will be retired from racing.

"It has been the honour of a lifetime to train a horse like Bow Echo. He has given us some extraordinary days and taken everyone involved on a journey we will never forget.

"To retire unbeaten, having won the 2000 Guineas, St James's Palace Stakes and Sussex Stakes says everything about what an exceptional racehorse he has been.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bow Echo and Gstaad served up a thriller in the St James's Palace Stakes on day one of Royal Ascot

"Bow Echo's remarkable story began with his owner-breeder, the late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid and it is a great sadness that he was not here to see what a lifetime of breeding was able to produce.

"Bow Echo's unbelievable constitution and extraordinary ability have set him apart. We will all miss seeing him at home and on the racecourse but we are incredibly excited for his next chapter and in time, to see a new generation of his progeny on the racecourse."

Sports.content:
Chelsea have made a new enquiry about signing Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly.

The Blues have a long-term interest in the midfielder and have made another check on his availability following Arsenal's signing of Bruno Guimaraes.

However, Arsenal do not want to sell Lewis-Skelly to a local rival and a team they may have to compete with for the top places this season. Chelsea were linked with Lewis-Skelly in January.

Manchester United also have a long-term interest in Lewis-Skelly. However, United are still deciding whether they will commit to signing another midfielder or a left-back before the deadline.

It is questionable whether United would be able to do any more significant deals should they make a move for Lewis-Skelly.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking in May, Lewis-Skelly said celebrating with the fans meant everything as Arsenal showcased the Premier League trophy around north London

This is amid a market of high prices for central-midfield players this summer, although he can play both positions.

Last season, Arsenal kept their squad together despite a big spend. They want to be ambitious again this summer - but there is an acceptance there will have to be sales.

Players like Ethan Nwaneri and Lewis-Skelly would represent pure profit.

Analysis: Would Arsenal be right to sell Lewis-Skelly?

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

"Pure profit" wrote Myles Lewis-Skelly on his Instagram page as Arsenal celebrated the Premier League title. Reading between the lines, it was message over his future.

Despite posing with the Premier League title in May, Lewis-Skelly had a very difficult campaign. Fully fit the whole season, he made just one Premier League start before Christmas - by the start of May he had only managed three.

Many fans felt it was right for Arsenal to move Lewis-Skelly on as the sale of an academy graduate would bring a 'pure profit' funds into the club - hence the message on Instagram.

But everything changed in May, Mikel Arteta put Lewis-Skelly in a previously unused midfield role for a crucial title run-in game against Fulham, and Arsenal got some life back into their team.

With Martin Zubimendi fading in terms of fitness and form - and Arsenal struggling against the Man City title race momentum - Lewis-Skelly was Man of the Match in the 3-0 win that put them back on track for the title.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Monday Night Football, Thierry Henry analysed Myles Lewis Skelly's outstanding midfield performance against Fulham.

Lewis-Skelly did not leave the midfield for the rest of the run-in - including the Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain.

From third choice left-back to playing in Arsenal's biggest game in 20 years, Lewis-Skelly had kick-started his Arsenal career again. But now the question marks have returned.

The £75m signing of Bruno Guimaraes has threatened his role in the Arsenal midfield. The Gunners' two most expensive players are now the Brazilian and Declan Rice.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes come face-to-face for the first time after the Brazilian made his move from Newcastle to the Premier League champions.

For two midfield positions, Arsenal have Rice, Guimaraes, Lewis-Skelly, Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Five does not go into two, so does something - or someone in this instance - have to give?

Ever since his breakthrough last year, Lewis-Skelly has become a fan favourite at Arsenal. He has showed his ability in both midfield and left-back - it is worth remembering he played 180 minutes in defence as Arsenal beat Real Madrid in the Champions League in 2025.

There are valid reasons for Arsenal keeping a hold on Lewis-Skelly, particularly given the amount of minutes key midfielder Rice has played over the past year.

The 27-year-old played in all but two of the Premier League, Champions League and Carabao Cup games between January 1 and the end of the season.

Image: Minutes played by Arsenal players in midfield

By the time Rice got to the World Cup, England manager Thomas Tuchel admitted the midfielder was in "a lot of pain". Rice was substituted regularly during the World Cup - something that very rarely happens in an Arsenal shirt.

The sheer amount of minutes he has played means Arsenal cannot rely on the midfielder to just carry on running through the barriers. If Rice is to be rotated more often, then that opens the door for Lewis-Skelly to continue playing.

But on the flip side, Arsenal have Zubimendi and Merino as options for Rice rotation. And with Arsenal needing to address others areas and showing a need to sell better - their record transfer sale is still Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain's £35m move to Liverpool in 2017 - then Lewis-Skelly's future opens up a conundrum.

Arteta said important decisions will need to be made this summer to take the team to another level. But a popular academy graduate ends up at a Premier League rival, then that is not just an important decision - it's a controversial one.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 5: Brighton
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 9th (NB: this is not necessarily John Brewin’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 8th

Prospects

Last season’s final day in May featured Brighton fans and players united in celebrating qualification for the Europa Conference League despite losing 3-0 to Manchester United. Considering West Ham and Crystal Palace have won the competition since its inception, lifting that trophy becomes a target to aim for.

How realistic is that? Beyond the Thursday-Sunday schedule playing in the Conference League demands, it has been a summer of change within the ranks. James Milner did not celebrate as Europe was reached. By then he had decided he would retire. Danny Welbeck was last season’s outstanding forward for Brighton, one of the best in England, and has followed the now traditional trade route to Chelsea. Him turning 36 in November adds a note of curiosity to that transfer. Thus, the veteran class, each older than their head coach, Fabian Hürzeler, still just 33, is reduced to Pascal Gross, Lewis Dunk and the reserve goalkeeper Jason Steele. Solly March not being offered a new contract was another break from the past, a surprise to a long-serving and popular player whose injury problems counted against him.

Jan Paul van Hecke, last season’s best defender, has been sold to Tottenham for £52m, with the teenager Luka Vuskovic coming in the opposite direction. If Brighton supporters are wondering about their club’s slew of new signings then their Premier League peers will be watching as closely, such is the industry’s respect for the club’s recruitment. The Jamestown Analytics company owned by Tony Bloom, Brighton’s financier, is a football Rosetta Stone, admired and coveted. It is not, though, completely infallible; there have been a number of busts.

Fans hugely enjoyed being in the Europa League three seasons ago, reaching the last 16, but it had a deleterious effect at home, stretching resources and relations with the then manager, Roberto De Zerbi. Brighton finished a disappointing 11th. Better is hoped for this time around.

Off-field picture

Safe standing is being expanded in the South Stand of the Amex, as part of a £40m modernisation project. The work will take place during September’s extended international break and is a drive towards enhancing the atmosphere. The ownership is among the most mindful of the matchday experience in English football. For Albion fans seeking a middle ground between the posh seats and pre-match drinks in the concourse, there’s the opening of the 1901 Pub, a “hybrid traditional pub and premium matchday lounge designed for a more relaxed fan experience”. With a capacity of 660, membership starts at £173 a month.

Owner-fan relationship

There can be no doubt that Brighton’s continued success relies on the patronage and funds of Bloom. The club’s supporters are more than aware of this. Last season, Bloom’s involvement with Hearts’ chase for the Scottish title demonstrated he has wider horizons, though his key priority will always be the hometown, boyhood club. In January, “the Lizard”, as he is known in the gambling circles he made his fortune, increased his Brighton investment with a £107m loan, making for an overall loan amount of £400m. Without Bloom’s financing and his continued enthusiasm, Brighton would not be the established, model Premier League force they remain.

The manager

Hürzeler has done much growing up in public. There have been points during his two seasons when doubts circled. In the boardroom, though, Bloom and his influential chief executive, Paul Barber, have kept faith in the still youthful Bavarian. As a new, three-year contract was announced in May, Bloom referred to a “clear playing identity”. Hürzeler can be fiery. His touchline behaviour does not always meet the approval of officials and opposing coaches but he enters the season as the fifth longest-serving manager in the Premier League and will be showing off a severe hair remodelling unveiled in pre-season. Success in European football can burnish a growing reputation.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen New arrival Luka Vuskovic’s playmaking abilities from the back are highly regarded. Photograph: Matt Impey/Shutterstock

Will Tottenham rue never drawing on Vuskovic’s potential? Brighton hope so. He never played a match for Spurs but impressed on loan at Hamburg, where his reading of the game, positioning and maturity drew rave reviews. The signing of the experienced centre-back Pascal Struijk from Leeds means Vuskovic can be allowed time to develop but the Croatian’s playmaking abilities from the back may make him a long-term successor for the captain, Dunk. His fee, reported at £46m when Spurs paid £12m for him, suggests the demand for his talents. The hope and expectation is that the deal becomes regarded as a bargain.

Stat attack

The two Manchester clubs were the only sides who scored more Premier League goals than Brighton in regular play last season. The Seagulls dropped down the standings a little once counterattacks were included but they had an identical rate for open play expected goals per game as Arsenal in 2025-26. There should be no shortage of chances for whoever picks up the goalscoring baton after Danny Welbeck’s departure.

Set for a breakthrough

Patience with new arrivals is part of the Brighton doctrines, players are given latitude and opportunity to bed in. A season’s grace is often granted, and Charalampos Kostoulas showed a few flashes of his talent during the 2025-26 campaign. With Welbeck departed, there is a vacancy to lead the line. The Greece international scored a brilliant overhead kick against Bournemouth in January, and at 19, last summer’s signing from Olympiakos should receive more airtime than the two league starts he received last season. His Greek compatriot Stefanos Tzimas, back in training after an ACL rupture, can provide either competition or a partnership.

World Cup impact

When Jordan Henderson played master of ceremonies as England celebrated third place at the World Cup, he made sure Steele was given a medal for his acclaimed, appreciated work as training goalkeeper. It was an otherwise mixed summer for Albion players, with Maxim De Cuyper going furthest to the quarter-finals with Belgium. Diego Gómez was suspended for Paraguay’s historic defeat of Germany though featured in his country’s bruising exit at the hands of France. Yasin Ayari became the first Brighton player to score two World Cup goals in a game as Sweden beat Tunisia 5-1. Michael Svoboda, the summer defensive signing from Venezia, did not play a single minute for Austria.

Sports.title: Infantino’s opponents developing new framework for running world football
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino’s opponents are working together to produce a new framework for running world football to replace what they regard as a system of patronage that Fifa has adopted since he replaced Sepp Blatter as president 10 years ago.

Repeated calls from Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation for an independent review of Fifa’s governance have been ignored by Infantino since his plan to sell off 21% of the World Cup was made public a fortnight ago, and the rebels are now understood to have taken matters into their own hands.

A source with knowledge of the discussions told the Guardian that the three confederations are working on producing a policy document to demonstrate how the world governing body could evolve in the future.

Those involved have been empowered to ask existential questions such as what Fifa’s precise role should be, how it should be structured and what governance model should be adopted. Financial distribution among member associations is also a key consideration, particularly with an eye on how best to deploy funds from Fifa’s estimated $5bn (£3.7bn) reserves.

If Infantino refuses to engage then the new framework is likely to be adopted by a challenger at the presidential election next year, or could even serve as a template for a breakaway organisation.

After releasing a joint statement on Monday, which called for “leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it”, Uefa, Concacaf and the AFC let it be known that they have begun preliminary discussions about organising new competitions if the standoff with Fifa’s leadership persists.

View image in fullscreen Uefa officials are meeting in Salzburg where the Super Cup takes place on Wednesday between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa. Photograph: Gintare Karpaviciute/Reuters

At present the Under-20 Women’s World Cup next month could take place without European teams, as Uefa is maintaining that its members will boycott the tournament, unless Fifa moves quickly to set up an independent review of the World Cup sell‑off debacle and provide legally binding assurances that such a move will not be repeated.

The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, is seen as the most likely presidential challenger to Infantino at this stage – although, as he told the Guardian in June, his current focus is on being reelected as president of the North and Central American confederation next year.

It seemed significant, however, that the joint statement released on Monday contained strong echoes of a speech given by Montagliani at the Fifa congress this year in Vancouver, where he said: “Let me be frank, leadership is not about power.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Senior figures from European football are gathering in person for the first time since the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal broke, with a number of meetings expected in Salzburg – where the Uefa Super Cup final will be held on Wednesday – over the next two days.

The Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, will hold talks with Nasser al-Khelaifi, the chair of European Football Clubs, aimed at reinforcing the continent’s unity in demanding a change at the top of Fifa.

Uefa continues to hold firm in its pledge to boycott Fifa competitions, having not received its desired assurances that there will be no recurrence of the issues that caused the current crisis.

Sports.title: Emery positive about Aston Villa’s outlook despite summer exits as PSG await
Sports.content:
One thing was almost instantly detectable as Unai Emery walked into a stuffy room inside the Red Bull Arena on the eve of Wednesday’s Super Cup against Paris Saint-Germain. After a summer of change, Aston Villa’s manager appeared uber-relaxed, confident his team will absorb a series of headline departures. He cracked a joke about his English improving and poked fun at John McGinn, impersonating his captain while next to him on the auditorium’s top table.

Emery was in a jovial mood, then. But he was also switched on, alert to the frequency, the tone of the wave of questions at the beginning of his fourth full season in the job. “You ask about the changes of coaches and players, but McGinn is intelligent and his answer was fantastic,” Emery said with a smile. “When he arrived here [in 2018] they were in the Championship and every year since there have been changes and still the club has moved forward.

“If we compare ourselves to other clubs like Man City, Chelsea, Manchester United, Arsenal and Liverpool, we are competing with them. We don’t have their power … yet.”

Emery spoke with an enthusiasm that will be music to the ears of Villa supporters fretting about the size of the task on his hands. Villa have sold Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, the latter returning to PSG, for whom he could make his second debut against his former club. Villa would be tested again if Arsenal make a serious play for Ezri Konsa, who, together with Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martínez, remains on holiday after World Cup duty. Three key coaching staff have also left, including the set-piece coach, Austin MacPhee. But Emery, the beating heart of the operation, as McGinn said, is still in the building.

McGinn’s response was punchy when asked where expectations should be for the forthcoming campaign. “Similar to where it has been in the past few seasons,” he said. “I think we have consistently competed with the best in England, the best in Europe, no matter what the competition is. We will have our challenges. There is a lot of change, but when you look at other clubs around England there is a lot of change there as well: a lot of coaches changing, a lot of players changing.

“But what we still have is our main core, same manager, same methods, same desire to achieve more. A lot of people thought we had reached our ceiling a couple of seasons ago, and we proved them wrong. We have still got the same hunger and desire to go and achieve more. Our job is just to integrate the new players and try and make them believe, in the same way the players in the last few seasons have believed. I’m really excited by the sort of ‘new Aston Villa’.”

View image in fullscreen Players and staff of Aston Villa on the pitch at Stadion Salzburg. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

Villa, of course, did not want to lose Rogers. Chelsea paid £117m to sign the England midfielder, two and a half years after Emery asked Villa to pay £8m to take him from Middlesbrough. The same goes for Tielemans, who after a slow start established himself as one of Emery’s undroppables. Villa signed Tielemans on a free but sold the 29‑year‑old for £35m. Digne was an equally reliable performer, taking back the left-back spot from £38m buy Ian Maatsen.

Emery knows the business but it was particularly interesting to hear him talk about the importance of the leverage Villa have gained off the back of the ride they have been on over the past few years. One of the most memorable nights was their pulsating quarter-final against PSG 16 months ago, a 3-2 second‑leg victory at Villa Park, when Gianluigi Donnarumma pulled off three superb saves to prevent Villa taking the game to extra time. Emery ended up on all fours after Willian Pacho blocked Maatsen’s goal-bound volley with 28 seconds to play.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The Premier League is the best league in the world and Aston Villa can now have better brands in the way we are,” Emery said. “I am so, so, so happy how the club is committed together with us. [I am so happy] with how we are getting better, keeping our consistency in the Premier League … the club is making a huge effort to try to be in the same direction as me. They are trying to extend Villa Park to achieve 50,000 supporters next season. We are increasing our budget through good results on the pitch, by sometimes selling some players and being consistent like we are, and as well expecting a high level, like we are more or less keeping.”

Emery, who spent two years in charge of PSG, knows how these things work. PSG are no longer just a football team but a brand: see their megastore on London’s Oxford Street. PSG’s chief executive, Victoriano Melero, has talked of PSG competing with the likes of Real Madrid on the pitch but labels like the LA Lakers and Ferrari off it.

Salzburg is the latest destination on Villa’s quest for success, with 6,000 Villa fans in tow. The stadium facade is plastered with images of McGinn and co celebrating their Europa League win in Istanbul in May. “I am feeling comfortable, happy, very demanding, even more than the last years,” Emery said. “We want more. We are not stopping here.”

Sports.title: Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly offered to Manchester United as left-back solution
Sports.content:
Myles Lewis-Skelly has been offered to Manchester United as a potential left-back option, with Arsenal wishing to recoup some of the £75m paid to Newcastle for Bruno Guimarães.

Chelsea, it is understood, have also been made aware of the 19-year-old’s availability. Lewis-Skelly won the Premier League under Mikel Arteta last term, but whether the west London club will make a move for him is unclear.

Lewis-Skelly, who made only five league starts and 36 appearances in all competitions in 2025-26, signed a five-year contract last summer. His prospective price is thought to be in the region of £45m.

This is within the range of finance United have spent so far this summer, after Youri Tielemans’s £35m move from Aston Villa and Andrey Santos’s arrival for £48m plus £2m of add-ons from Chelsea. United are now weighing up a move for the teenager.

Newcastle’s Lewis Hall remains of prime interest for United but, after losing Guimarães, Sandro Tonali to Tottenham, and Anthony Gordon to Barcelona, the new Newcastle manager, Matthias Jaissle, is intent the 21-year-old England international does not also depart

RB Leipzig’s 28-year-old left-back David Raum is another in the position United may assess.

Chelsea have already had a busy summer in the market, having spent over £300m on a raft of new signings. Maxence Lacroix and Marco Palestra have been brought in to bolster the centre and right of the defence respectively, while Morgan Rogers became the club’s record signing at a cost of £117m.

But Xabi Alonso’s side have a hole on the left of their defence after Marc Cucurella’s £52m move to Real Madrid. The 20-year-old Jorrel Hato, who featured for the Netherlands at the World Cup, was Cucurella’s deputy at left-back.

Mason Mount missed training on Monday and Tuesday at United’s County Kildare summer training camp owing to a knock he received on a foot in Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg.

The the 27-year-old midfielder being stood down is a precautionary measure, it is understood, and he is also set to sit out Wednesday’s penultimate pre-season friendly against Leeds at Croke Park. The game at the 81,300 capacity venue is a sell-out.

United’s final friendly before Michael Carrick’s team start the season on Saturday week at Hull is against Milan in Wroclaw on Saturday.

Sports.title: Djed Spence nears Tottenham exit with Inter in talks over £25.6m move
Sports.content:
Tottenham are prepared to allow Djed Spence to join Inter, with the England defender expected to cost around €30m (£25.6m).

Spence – who started four games at the World Cup, including the semi-final against Argentina – has fallen further down the pecking order at Spurs after the arrival of Andy Robertson from Liverpool. He signed a new four‑year contract in north London at the start of last season but is believed to be keen on joining the Italian champions, with Destiny Udogie and Pedro Porro expected to be Roberto De Zerbi’s preferred full‑backs this season.

Talks are ongoing over a fee for the 26-year-old as Inter search for a replacement for Denzel Dumfries, who joined Real Madrid this summer. But personal terms are not believed to be an issue and an agreement is likely to be reached that will see Inter pay only slightly more than the £20m fee Spurs paid to sign Spence from Middlesbrough in 2022.

Inter also held talks with Tottenham over a potential move for Cristian Romero but the Argentina defender looks poised to join Atlético Madrid for a fee of €40m. They have yet to agree a fee but Romero is expected to move to La Liga despite interest from elsewhere, including the Premier League champions Arsenal.

On Monday, Spurs – who have spent almost £240m this summer on new players, including Sandro Tonali for a club‑record £92.5m, confirmed that Micky van de Ven has signed a new five-year contract. “It’s clear the direction the club wants to go in and I want to be a part of it. I’m excited about what’s to come,” the Netherlands defender said.

Crystal Palace, meanwhile, are in talks to re-sign Evann Guessand on a season-long loan from Aston Villa. The Côte d’Ivoire forward spent the second half of last season at Selhurst Park and was part of the side that won the Conference League in May, although Palace decided not to take up an option to sign him earlier in the summer. The south London club are also expected to complete deals for Anan Khalaili from Union Saint‑Gilloise for £21m and Zavier Gozo from Real Salt Lake for £11m.

Sports.title: ‘I am quite optimistic’: Newcastle’s Jaissle on leading club after turbulent summer
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle has been described as “fire” and a “rockstar”, but his formal “unveiling” as Newcastle’s manager revealed a rather more considered and conservative character than advertised.

At the precise moment the clock struck 3pm on Tuesday the 38‑year‑old German walked into a packed media suite at St James’ Park. Before taking his seat on the stage Jaissle, wearing a smartly understated open-necked suit complete with a silk pocket square, took a deep breath and jumped down into audience, making a point of shaking everyone’s hand. It was a courteous and classy gesture.

Once back on that podium, his evident excitement at exchanging Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ahli for the Premier League was tempered by the sort of realism inevitable at a club that, in Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães, has just sold its three best players.

“This is now a vacuum as you call it,” Eddie Howe’s successor said in his excellent English. “They were great characters, great players, ­experienced players. Obviously we are in that transition phase. My job is to make the best out of it all. I am quite optimistic. We are ambitious, that’s the most important thing and why I decided to come here. But it will not happen overnight. I’m pretty sure it will be a successful story. But we need time now.”

Regular chats with the England head coach, Thomas Tuchel, promise to help minimise any culture shock. “It’s been a long connection,” he said. “Thomas was my youth coach when I was a youth player at Stuttgart. He was amazing, I really admire him.

“He’s a really special coach and I’m looking forward to staying in touch with him, and getting insights on the league. That’s something I want to use for sure. But it’s also important to build your own opinions because every coach is their own human being and has their opinions and, ­sometimes players get stuck in a box. It’s ­important for me to be neutral about players.”

Allied to a willingness to chall­enge assumptions, such refusal to take labels at face value hinted at the qualities that prompted David ­Hopkinson, Newcastle’s Canadian chief executive, to dub Jaissle “fire” and “a rock star”.

View image in fullscreen Newcastle beat Valencia 2-1 in Jaissle’s first pre-season game in charge. Photograph: Clive Brunskill/Getty Images

If the one-time RB Salzburg manager’s brand of football – “front foot, intense, aggressive, vertical and, of course, also successful” – fits the latter tag, Newcastle fans have greeted him with an adaptation of a late 1970s Euro-disco hit.

Where the Spanish female pop duo Baccara soared to No 1 with Yes, Sir I Can Boogie, travelling supporters attending the friendly win in Valencia last Saturday chorused: “Oh Jaissle I can boogie/You try me once, you’ll beg for more.”

Jaissle said: “All my staff members already said they’re looking forward to sitting after a match in the bar and listening to the song. So let’s see about that! I heard it once and I was smiling. I’m really happy the fans already appreciate me a lot. The welcome from the fans was unbelievable when I was having a walk yesterday in the city. It was really giving me a nice feeling.”

There were more “big smiles” when he recalled a phone call last month asking him if he would be interested in replacing Howe but, little more than 48 hours after arriving in Newcastle for the first time following a training camp at La Manga in southern Spain, Jaissle is under no illusions as to the scale of the challenge ahead.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

With the need to comply with football’s spending rules having seen the club pivot to buying young players with high resale potential – four of their five summer signings so far are aged 20 or younger – the immediate future remains opaque.

“I’m long enough in the industry now that you cannot promise anything,” Jaissle said when asked what he aimed to achieve this season. “It makes no sense to promise you things now because I don’t know how things will look in one year. But it doesn’t make sense to see the negative. There will be more adjustments to the squad this summer. We still have time. I would say keep the optimism.”

His cautiously upbeat mood will be bolstered further should Newcastle’s ongoing talks with Benfica about potentially signing their 23‑year‑old full-back Amar Dedic, who played for Jaissle at Salzburg and can operate on both the right and the left, conclude successfully.

“I had a tour of St James’ Park two days ago,” Jaissle said. “When I entered the pitch here with my assistant coaches for the first time, we were looking at each other with smiles and goosebumps. It’s really special, an amazing stadium. I can’t wait to see it full.

“When I received the call at the end of July and it was clearly most likely Eddie would quit there were no doubts or question marks. I had a big smile.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Liverpool, Jeff Bezos and mission creep off the field at Anfield
Sports.content:
THIS MEANS MORE (MONEY)

Far be it for Football Daily to make cheap gags [wait, what? – Football Daily Ed] relating to the involvement of Amazon founder and master of the universe Jeff Bezos in a consortium buying around 30% of Liverpool FC. Will new signings arrive via prompt delivery but end up next door at Everton? How will fans rate the packaging? Etc, etc. There’s also the involvement of Eduardo Saverin, the Facebook co-founder poking his head in. Though long ago unfriended by Mark Zuckerberg, Saverin still ranked No 56 on Forbes’s billionaires list. These are seriously rich men, and among the planet’s chino class, to quote Vladimir Putin, “soccer is popular”. The Geopolitics World Cup posh seats were full of those eyeing up deals on a frontier hardly new to investors from the USA USA USA, but where there may be much more gold to strike. See Gianni Infantino’s misreading of the art of the deal as an, ahem, prime example.

Bezos is no football man, barely known as a sports fan. Links with buying the Seattle Seahawks, his local NFL franchise, were speculative. He is, though, the third richest man in the world, according to appendage-measuring listicles. Amazon’s market value is higher than Brazil’s annual GDP. For certain people, that triggers arousal at the thought of their team being able to buy the biggest and best players in the world. Just imagine if their club was to spend, say, £446m in a single summer. How good would that be?

For others, there is a regrettable mission creep towards a civic institution – one that, despite global fame, cleaves to its local community – being tossed around by venture capitalists. Though that process has been in train since Tom Hicks and George Gillett arrived on Merseyside, full of huckster charm, almost two decades ago. The socialism and collectivism Bill Shankly envisaged for the club he made famous disappeared in the sepia-tinged rearview mirror. Football was a business even back in Shanks’ day but now attracts the richest suits of all; if Bezos is chancing his arm in football, what price Elon Musk or Google tycoon Larry Page are seen wearing the scarf of their chosen club? Oh joy.

Current overlords Fenway Sports Group, who picked up the pieces from impending disaster in 2010, are, yes, a consortium of American venture capitalists. Their existential aim is to make as much loot as possible from an asset purchased for a knockdown price of £300m. It’s gone well. This mooted deal includes Bezos, Saverin and Amit Bhatia, a frontman you may recognise from when QPR fans celebrated their owners being richer than Roman Abramovich. That did not go well. The latest deal would value the club at £4.4bn. High-fives all round, though the doubles and trebles may take time. Liverpool enter the season with an imbalanced squad, unsuited to a manager whose arrival was generally seen as a Good Thing. If football is all about money, even the biggest money cannot solve every problem.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“After careful consideration, we don’t feel it is right to proceed at this time without the necessary preparation in place, but we will remain in conversation with the club and see what is possible in the future” – one wealthy benefactor not entering the game – yet – is Turki Alalshikh, whose bid to buy a controlling interest in Derby will no longer proceed, with the club now off the market.

RECOMMENDED LOOKING

Here’s David Squires on … the masochistic life of a Football League fan.

View image in fullscreen Illustration: David Squires/The Guardian

double quotation mark Having also boycotted the GWC and also being very concerned about the season to come, I sympathise with Ken Muir (yesterday’s Football Daily letters). But at least Hearts know who their manager is. Due to the absurd, months-long FA ‘investigation’ into the manager who’s clearly admitted culpability for the undisputed facts of Spygate, my club, Southampton, is in a horrid limbo. Surely it could have been done and dusted in a couple of weeks and Saints could have planned accordingly. But perhaps the FA blazers were too busy writing their letter of support to Gianni Infantino to worry about destabilising my football club” – Bob Cushion.

double quotation mark ‘It’s 15 years of frustration here at this club,’ says Rangers boss Derek McInnes (yesterday’s Quote of the Day.) Steven Gerrard and the sole object in his managerial trophy cabinet would like a word, Derek” – David Maddock.

double quotation mark Given the surfeit of the recent GWC machinations, the blatherings and canvassing for Gianni to do one (or not) and the less-than-sportsmanlike attitude from members of the Argentina team, can we please have a reprise of the Football Daily’s erstwhile, eventually abortive, attempt to ‘STOP FOOTBALL’? It has to be worth a thought, before VAR, PGMOL and Arsenal’s Dark Arts Department™ get to work on the 2026-27 Premier League shenanigans, surely?” – Budgie Wright.

Sports.title: Chelsea face Real Sociedad in WCL third qualifying round with riches at stake
Sports.content:
Chelsea will face Real Sociedad in the Women’s Champions League third qualifying round, needing a win over two legs to secure a place in the main league phase of the competition.

The 2021 runners-up and six-time European semi-finalists are taking part in the qualifying stage by virtue of their disappointing third-placed finish in the Women’s Super League last season – their lowest league ­finish since 2019 – and they will be the favourites against the Spanish side.

Chelsea could have faced Ajax, Inter, Eintracht Frankfurt or the ­Austrian side St Pölten. They were unable to meet the big-name sides such as Real Madrid, Wolfsburg, Juventus or Paris Saint-Germain at this stage because of seedings. Sonia Bompastor’s team will hope to join Arsenal and Manchester City in the main phase of the competition.

The potential financial implications of missing out on ­qualification are significant. All 18 clubs that take part in the league phase will receive a guaranteed minimum of €505,000 (£431,500), plus a further €60,000 for every league‑phase fixture they win and €20,000 for every draw, as well as prize money ranging from €10,000 to €180,000 depending on where they finish in the table, rising by €10,000 per position.

Additionally, the eventual champions will receive €1,050,000 in prize money across the course of the knockout phase – including €500,000 specifically for winning the final – as there are six-figure sums on offer for each knockout-phase fixture.

Chelsea will be at home for the first leg, which is scheduled to be played on 26 August, with the second leg in Spain scheduled for 2 September, three days before Chelsea’s WSL season opener, which is at home against Aston Villa on 5 September.

Chelsea have been strong contenders for the European title in recent years, reaching the semi-finals in three of the past four campaigns, but they lost to their rivals Arsenal in a dramatic quarter-final last term.
